sections.heading: Questions we get on the first call
items: How fast do you respond to a service call?

Same day, in all four territories, for devices under a Kelly service agreement. Technicians carry parts for the models we sell. Our NPS of 94.4 is audited by an independent third party, so that claim is checked by someone other than us.
Can you take over devices we bought from someone else?

Often, yes. The assessment covers your whole fleet regardless of where it came from, and the plan tells you honestly which devices are worth keeping under service and which are costing more than they are worth.

Depends on volume, cash preference and how fast your needs change. The plan prices all three side by side for your actual usage so you can compare, and rentals cover seasonal peaks without a long commitment.
Do you serve offices outside the Triad and Charlotte?

Our four locations cover the Triad, Charlotte and the Triangle, and customers with field offices across North Carolina are served from the nearest branch. If you are further afield, ask your nearest branch.

sections.heading: Request an assessment
sections.body: Tell us a little about your office and the nearest branch will call to set a time.
sections.note: A person from the nearest branch replies, not an autoresponder.

heard: Green and navy are the brand; the logo carries both, and it is built for a dark ground, so the header and footer are navy in every direction.
Your existing customers come to the site to request service, send meter reads and order supplies. Those stay one click from the top of every page.
Six service lines plus mailing all survive. Pure Technology (water, ice, coffee) is a revenue line, not a footnote.
The tone is approachable authority: proof points over hype, North Carolina references, urgent but not pushy.
Cross-sell is the growth plan: the site has to sell IT and document management to existing copier customers, not only copiers to strangers.
found: About 80% of your organic visits are people searching your name. The site is a phone book for people who already know you.
The only page earning strangers today is the Charlotte location page. Location pages are not optional; they are your non-branded traffic, so every direction has a real locations page.
The blog ranks 24 to 94 on real terms and is thin. It is the growth lever, so the blog matches the theme in every direction.
There is nothing to download or try for a visitor who is not ready to call. We would productize the assessment your MPS page already describes.
There is effectively no photography of your people or your four offices. A half-day shoot per office is the single thing that makes the site un-copyable.
Your assessment process, staged, is the differentiator. We built it as a five-stage section; we would like your real stage names and what each one hands the customer.
pick_reasons: Your brand voice is approachable authority
Clean is the plainest-spoken of the three: a humanist sans, generous white space, one action per section.
You have 4,000 customers using the site as a tool
Clean puts the customer fast lane and the phone number where they are found first, and stays fast to scan on a phone.
Clean gives the navy the chrome and the green the actions, so both brand colours do real work instead of competing.
pitch.pick_change: Clean's type can read a little quiet on the home page. We would borrow Showcase's larger heading scale for the hero and the section openers, and keep Clean's rhythm everywhere else.
alternatives: If you want the site to say modern dealer moving into IT first: same ground, a display typeface, wider measure and bigger rhythm.
If heritage is the story: an editorial serif on warm paper, the narrowest measure and the most catalogue-like. Nobody in your category looks like this.
plan: Choose a direction. Confirm the promise, the tagline, the location list and the BBB wording. Send the logo as a vector.
Copy for every page, from your service leadership and from you, in your words. Photography scheduled.
Build in your HubSpot: theme cloned and re-skinned, blog templates assigned, every page built, forms wired to named people.
Quality gate on every page, on a real phone. Redirects tested. You edit a page yourself in the walkthrough.
Go live. Reads at 30, 60 and 90 days against the baseline, with what we would change next.
pitch.heard_intro: We have not interviewed you yet. Everything here comes from your current site and your brand profile. Tell us if any of it is wrong; it outranks our house defaults.
confirm: The response commitment: what you promise today, and for which agreements. The pages say same-day under a Kelly agreement; the exact terms are yours to state.
The BBB wording. We have written BBB-accredited since 1960, rated A+. Please confirm both halves.
The Ricoh standing. Your profile says sixth-largest Ricoh dealer in the Southeast; we left it off until Ricoh confirms it.
Manufacturer authorizations to show: Ricoh, Konica Minolta, Sharp, Brother, and whether Epson belongs on the list.
The location list and the headquarters. Your site lists Winston-Salem, Greensboro, Charlotte and Raleigh; an older profile lists Hickory and a Greensboro HQ.
The tagline. Moving Business Forward Since 1947 is on your site today; Office Technology Done Right Since 1947 has also been used.
The key markets. We show six; your site has five pages. Which list is current?
Your assessment process, stage by stage, and what each stage hands the customer. We drafted five stages; they are ours until you replace them.
The customer count and where they are: about 4,000, most in North Carolina, or nationwide?
Permission to use the four testimonials on your current site, and their spellings.
pitch.footer: Prepared for Claudia Coleman, Director of Marketing. Nothing here is live or indexed. Every number we could source comes from your current site, your brand profile or public data. Several service commitments on these pages (response time, the assessment report, the staged process) are our draft of what we think you do, and they are listed under To confirm. The photograph on the home page is a generated stand-in until your own photography exists; partner logos are the ones on your current site.
